fields.name: Blood
fields.evidence: Toolkit build, EoCClient.dll+0xA96FA0 (character branch of ecl::TLPreviewDummyHelpers::PrePrepareDummy): copied from float 0 of eoc::splatter::StateComponent (Blood in esv::splatter::SplatterState, Visual.h).

fields.name: Dirt
fields.evidence: Same function: copied from float 2 of eoc::splatter::StateComponent (Dirt) - floats 1 and 2 are swapped compared with esv::splatter::SplatterState, which is why that struct is not reused.

fields.name: Bruises
fields.evidence: Same function: copied from float 1 of eoc::splatter::StateComponent (Bruises). bg3.exe+0x196F710 passes +8 and +0xC (with +0 and +4) to the visual splatter update bg3.exe+0x196D540.

fields.name: Sweat
fields.evidence: Same function: copied from float 3 of eoc::splatter::StateComponent (Sweat).

fields.name: State
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x6D50D0 creates the component as 36 zero bytes (all 4 live instances are zero - clean characters). EoCClient.dll+0xA96FA0 fills floats 0..3 from the source character's eoc::splatter::StateComponent when the dummy is prepared; bg3.exe+0x196F710 (queries {this, ls::VisualComponent} with a modified-tag, and {eoc::splatter::UpdateAttachmetsRequestOneFrameComponent, this, ls::VisualComponent}) applies these four values to the dummy's visual and to its attachments.

fields.name: InitialState
fields.evidence: EoCClient.dll+0xA96FA0 writes the same four values a second time into floats 4..7 in the same order. Only that writer was seen, so 'initial' (the copy taken from the character, as opposed to the one a timeline splatter key may change) is an interpretation.

fields.name: field_20
fields.evidence: Zeroed as one 32-bit store by bg3.exe+0x6D50D0; never written by the dummy preparation; live 0. No reader found.

open_questions: Order of the four values relies on (a) the Toolkit build of the copy routine, which may differ from the game build, and (b) Script Extender's field order of esv::splatter::SplatterState. A live dummy of a bloodied character would settle it.
field_20: 4 bytes (float, or a bool with padding).
